key_insight: Settling spheroids transition from random orientation to broadside alignment, while lateral slip peaks when the alignment rate approaches the Kolmogorov rate.
engineering_relevance: A measured lateral-slip peak could constrain the inertial torque coefficient or turbulent dissipation rate when particle properties and forcing statistics are known.
method: Model overdamped orientation using an inertial-torque potential and stochastic forcing.
Use an exact Boltzmann distribution for isotropic white noise and a linear-response closure for finite correlation times.
Represent dissipation intermittency with a lognormal mixture of Boltzmann distributions.
evidence_signal: Tensor-forced simulations reproduce the nearly shape-independent slip-peak ratio, while comparisons with plate DNS distributions and published moments support intermittency-induced broadening.
watch_item: The finite-correlation-time closure is least accurate in the random-to-aligned crossover and assumes overdamped dynamics with quasi-static Stokes drag.
paper_title: Orientation and slip statistics of spheroids settling in turbulence
